newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel-will not pay any price for Dublin EMU deal.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-will not pay any price for Dublin EMU deal.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday evening that agreement on a stability pact in time for next week's Dublin summit would be desirable, but that he would not seek agreement at any cost.

Waigel said at the end of one-day talks aimed at agreeing a framework for maintaining fiscal discipline after the start of a single currency, that European Union members were still at odds on "two or three figures."

He added that agreement on the stability pact had to be seen as a single package together with the EMS 2 -- a new exchange rate system for nations that do not join the Euro in the first round -- and the legal framework for the launch of the Euro.

Touching on the main bone of contention between member states, Waigel said that definitions of exceptional circumstances that would allow a government to exceed its fiscal targets must be "calculable, clear and recognisable."
Germany has argued throughout that a numerical measure should be agreed to define an excessively bad recession that would allow a country to overshoot in its spending targets.
